messages:
jamie: FYI our nightly SAST/DAST run flagged ~120 findings but the evidence bundle is incomplete. scanner artifacts show KMS decrypt errors. anyone seen this before?
security-bot: [alert] nightly-scan-run #3062468099 - 120 findings; 18 artifacts failed to decrypt (error: KMS::AccessDenied). Links: https://ci.internal/nightly/3062468099
lucas: we rolled a small IAM/RBAC change to service-account-scanner yesterday evening to tighten keys. that likely removed the decrypt binding for the scanner SA. checking now.
jamie: ack. the missing artifacts are mostly auth/serialization traces — kinda important for triage. want a rollback?
lucas: can confirm the change touched role: roles/keystore.decrypter -> removed grant on keystore-prod. I can reapply the grant but want to avoid broad perms in prod.
sara: quick triage plan: 1) collect existing S3/CI logs (don't re-run scans yet), 2) grant minimal decrypt permission for scanner SA, 3) re-run single failing job to rehydrate evidence, 4) attach new evidence to vuln tickets and mark gaps in audit. also open an incident record since this impacts evidence retention.
mike: log snippet from the job: ```
[2026-03-23T02:14:01Z] scanner: retrieving artifact key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abc123
[2026-03-23T02:14:01Z] scanner: KMS Error: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/scanner-sa is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt
```
jamie: thanks. are there any quick mitigation scripts we can run to attach existing plaintext if any backup exists?
lucas: backup ciphertext only lives in CI artifact storage; we need KMS decrypt to produce plaintext. mitigation is temporary grant with condition limiting to the CI job principal and TTL. I can script a one-time allow: ```
aws kms grant --key-id abc123 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/scanner-sa --operations Decrypt --retiring-principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/lifecycle-ops
```
sara: +1 to limited grant. also record the action in keystore audit and create a signed justification. add this to the post-incident review: why RBAC change didn't hit the scanner owners.
oncall: i'm taking initial ownership for the incident ticket INC-2026-045. i'll coordinate rollback windows and org-wide notifications.
jamie: owners for remediation: lucas takes the RBAC rollback/grant script, mike will re-run the failing scan job and verify artifacts, sara will update incident and file postmortem checklist. i'll update vuln triage to mark affected findings as "evidence-missing" until re-run.
mike: when i re-run, do you want me to run a single repo job or full matrix? prefer single repo (auth-service) first.
sara: single repo first, collect evidence, then expand if needed. also add an entry to the secure-sdlc checklist: "on RBAC keystore changes notify scanner owners 24h prior".
lucas: pushing a limited grant now, ETA ~3m. will add an expiry tag.
security-bot: [audit] kms.grant created by lucas at 2026-03-23T02:20:11Z (grant-id: g-0a1b2c)
mike: re-run kicked off: https://ci.internal/job/scan/auth-service/3871
mike: re-run completed, artifacts present. sample evidence attached to ticket. no new findings introduced by the re-run.
jamie: great — update: INC-2026-045 created and linked to the vuln tracker. action items: (1) lucas rotate to a least-privilege workflow for scanner (2) sara run postmortem w/ timeline (3) engineering leads to add RBAC notification to change process. target: complete by EOD.
oncall: logged updates, tagging @eng-leads. I'll run the oncall wrap-up in 4h.
sara: draft postmortem template notes: cause = RBAC change removed KMS decrypt binding for scanner SA; impact = missing evidence for 18 artifacts in nightly SAST/DAST; remediation = temporary grant + re-run scans; follow-ups = change control update, owner notify, add CI-level smoke-test for decrypt.
jamie: thanks team. leaving the thread open until postmortem is published. :thumbsup:
